scope: Account-scoped admission for authenticated API reads with safe UI recovery
before: The previous API returned a full KTP despite an exhausted seeded read budget
The previous Lite showed its login form after a temporary profile-read failure despite a valid session; the corrected regression test reproduced that state

implementation.algorithm: Atomic PostgreSQL GCRA admission; gradually replenished capacity without fixed-minute rollover
implementation.key: Authenticated owner ID plus one of four fixed categories; never a caller-supplied IP or document ID
implementation.response: 429 READ_LIMIT, Retry-After seconds in header and JSON, no-store, localized message
implementation.writes: Existing write budgets remain separate; exhausted reads do not prevent canonical saves or account deletion
implementation.cleanup: At most four rows per account; foreign-key cascade removes them with the account

verification.tightenedParallelCase: Also passed in Chromium and WebKit with the exact elapsed-time upper bound: burst 6 plus floor(elapsedSeconds / 2)
verification.parallelReads: 24 simultaneous requests using different resource IDs share one bucket; real time restores admission, and subsequent denials leave the stored schedule unchanged
verification.isolation: Separate owners and work categories; ownership checks still reject foreign data
verification.ui: First material/profile load retries, no false guest page, two successful canonical saves while rereads are denied, editable fields preserved
verification.mobileAccessibility: 360 px and scoped axe checks for the main and Lite error messages
verification.legacyFirefox115: Actual ESR 115.40.0 completed import, compact backup, recovery, teacher approval and DOCX export on the current Windows host
verification.databaseRestore: All 21 public tables and all 11 migrations restored into a separate temporary database; content fingerprints matched, including api_read_budgets

limitations: Local synthetic data and local container build; no public cloud deployment or paid AI calls
Not a distributed load test or a physical Windows 7 performance benchmark
Public health/public-config and authentication use separate controls
Per-account rate limits do not establish a global memory ceiling or prevent distributed denial of service
Streaming large downloads, public-probe caching and continuous school-network load remain audit items
